- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–4% for next 7–14 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if recent 7-day avg is below 75.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a 30-day forecast, model often misses the turn; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model often fails to anticipate drop; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently above true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
